category_title: Students with personal, social, or academic challenges who prefer work-based learning
scenario_title: Discussing workplace culture and employment policies
minimal_context: The student is working in a group to draw up an employment policy based on theories of appreciation after watching a documentary about kitchen culture.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Now that we have watched the documentary about the kitchen at NOMA, please sit in your groups and draw up an employment policy connecting to the theories of appreciation.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I'm still shocked by that documentary. I feel really sorry for the apprentices in the kitchen and how they were yelled at if they made mistakes. But why do we have to write a policy document about theories?

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Just discuss what this could include for your future well-being at a workplace and write it down.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Well, respectful communication and a friendly tone are the most important, and maybe a rewarding salary. But I'm dreaming about a traineeship at a prestigious restaurant to be a chef, not sitting at a desk doing linguistic disciplines. This feels like irrelevant information.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: You need to complete the assignment. Please focus on applying the cognitive theories to the employment policy.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Pushes chair away from the group's desk loudly) I have a hard time just to sit and take in! This is just traditional cognitive-based teaching and has nothing to do with real kitchen work. I'm not doing this!
